thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update; ETFs, Stocks in the Red as Weakness in Tech Stocks Weigh on Broader Market

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update; ETFs, Stocks in the Red as Weakness in Tech Stocks Weigh on Broader Market
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Thursday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.3%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -0.5%
iPath S&P 500 VIX ST Futures ETN ( VXX ): +3.4%
ProShares Trust Ultra VIX Short Term Futures ETF ( UVXY ): +5.2%
VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF ( GDX ): -0.1%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was down 1.3%.
U.S. stocks were in negative territory at session's half, with tech stocks under selling pressure as the Congressional testimony by tech executives Sheryl Sandberg, COO of Facebook (FB), and Jack Dorsey of Twitter ( TWTR ) continued to weigh on the sector amid concerns Washington will enact regulations to restrain the social media industry.
Persistent fears of a protracted trade war between China and the U.S. and its likely impact on the global economy also overshadowed mostly bullish data.
The private sector added 163,000 new jobs in August, less than what was expected, and down from +219,000 in July. At the same time, jobless claims fell 10,000 in the latest survey week to 203,000, its lowest level in almost 50 years, and below 213,000 estimates.
Data from the services sector was mixed as the purchasing manager's index declined to 54.2 in August from the preliminary 55.2 and July's 56.0. But a comparable survey from the Institute for Supply Management jumped to 58.5 in August from 55.7 previously, beating Wall Street's 56.8 estimates.
On the manufacturing front, non-farm productivity was up 2.9% in the second quarter, while unit labor costs fell 1.0%. Factory orders fell a greater-than-expected 0.8% in July, but were up 0.2% excluding the transportation sector.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 1.1% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were in the red.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was down 1.8% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was down 2.4%.
The European Commission has cleared Apple's (AAPL) proposed acquisition of UK music discovery app Shazam, saying the deal would not adversely affect competition in the European Economic Area, according to Reuters. The commission launched a full-scale investigation into the transaction in April over concerns that technology companies like Apple could buy a data-rich competitor to mine it for information or drive others out of the market. AAPL shares fell nearly 2%.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs (XLF) was down 0.6%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 0.8% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 0.9%.
LaSalle Hotel Properties (LHO) fell some 1% after the firm agreed to be acquired by Pebblebrook Hotel Trust (PEB) for $37.80 in cash or for a fixed exchange ratio of 0.92 Pebblebrook common share for each share of LaSalle. Late Wednesday, LaSalle determined Pebblebrook's $5.2 billion offer was superior to Blackstone's (BX) final all-cash offer of $33.50 per share. Accordingly, LaSalle has terminated its previously announced merger agreement with affiliates of The Blackstone Group (BX). The private equity fund declined to rebid, taking its $112 million breakup fee. Following the close of the transaction, Pebblebrook will have a portfolio of 66 assets in or near 16 key urban markets, and will remain headquartered in Bethesda, MD. Jon Bortz will remain on as Pebblebrook chairman and CEO.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was down 1.6% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 1.5%.
Magellan Midstream Partners L.P (MMP) was down more than 1% after Reuters said the company projected that it would need to spend about $2 billion to construct a proposed crude oil pipeline from the Permian Basin in West Texas to the US Gulf Coast, Reuters reported. Magellan and co-investors Energy Transfer Partners (ETP), MPLX (MPLX) and Delek US Holdings (DK) will construct the pipeline, which is expected to start operations in mid-2020.
Commodities
Crude was down 2%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 2.7%. Natural gas was down 0.5% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 0.7%.
Gold was up 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.1%. Silver was up 0.4%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 0.3%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 0.1% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were weaker.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 0.4% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were lower.
The Buckle (BKE) fell nearly 7% after the retailer said net sales for the four-week period ended Sept. 1 slumped by 6.3% to $75.2 million from $80.3 million a year ago. Comparable-net sales for the same period slipped by 0.7%. Shares declined by more than 6.5% intraday. For the 30-week to Sept. 1, net sales fell by 1.4% to $481.2 million from $488.2 million a year earlier, according to a statement. Comparable net sales for the same period were also down 0.7%
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 0.5% and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 2%.
Amedica (AMDA) rose more than 6% after the company said it plans to sell its commercial spine business to closely held CTL Medical for up to $10 million and change its name. CTL Medical will own Amedica's metal and silicon nitride spine products and it plans to rename itself CTL Amedica, according to a statement on Thursday from Amedica. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter. With the sale Amedica will concentrate on its biomaterials and OEM business, the company said in the statement.
